Subject: Dedicated capacity: performance SLO follow-up and validation plan

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the performance/SLO items we discussed so your team can validate Dedicated capacity sizing: 

Summary of your targets I captured:
- P95 latency: <= 150 ms for responses up to ~256 tokens
- Streaming: yes — partial-token streaming required (first-byte target < 250 ms)
- Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent requests
- Sustained throughput: ~500 requests/min during business hours, with spiky bursts to ~750/min
- Model: Llama2-13B-chat (you mentioned the tuned variant)

What we need from you to run a focused validation:
1) A sample traffic shape (CSV) or a short trace of requests (timestamps, token counts) — helps pick batch sizing
2) Any hard constraints on cost or GPU types (preference for H100 vs A100)
3) Confirmation of a preferred 2-day window for a validation run (we typically do an isolated dedicated pool test)

What we'll provide:
- A sizing worksheet (attached) comparing H100 / A100 configs and estimated reserved throughput
- A validation run playbook (attached) that outlines test stages: synthetic baseline, live-sample replay, and streaming latency checks
- Recommended default: H100-backed Dedicated pool with shard sizing tuned for 13B chat; we'll provide reserved throughput and burst settings once we see traffic shape

Proposed next step: please share the sample traffic and confirm availability for a 2-day validation starting Mar 2 or Mar 3. If you prefer, we can do a quick 30-min tech sync to line up test cases.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this validated for you.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the targets and adding a few details from our side:
- P95 latency: 150 ms target for median-sized responses (~200–300 tokens). For longer responses (1k tokens) we expect p95 to be higher but would like guidance on where that lands.
- Streaming: important for UX; first-byte < 250 ms and steady partial updates thereafter (we measure on the client side).
- Concurrency: we expect peak concurrency of ~120 (spikes to 150 for brief periods)
- Throughput: sustained ~500 req/min, bursts to 750/min (as you captured)
- Model: Llama2-13B-chat (tuned by our data science team) — will provide the model artifact ID and tokenizer details once procurement clears
- Timeline: procurement expects an approved vendor by end of March; would appreciate a validation run this week or next to inform sizing in our SOW.

We're fine with Redwood recommending a GPU — cost is a factor but predictable performance is higher priority. We'll share a one-day sample trace (CSV) by EOD today.

Schedule: Mar 2 at 10:00 AM PST works for our engineering lead if you can confirm.

Best,

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: performance SLO follow-up and validation plan

Great — thanks for the quick reply and for committing the sample trace. A few follow-ups and our preliminary recommendation based on the targets you provided: 

Prelim GPU comparison (high level):
- H100 (NVL): best raw throughput for 13B chat with fp16 / nf4 quantization, lower tail latency under heavy concurrency; higher cost but most predictable for streaming and high concurrency.
- A100 80GB: strong option for lower cost than H100 for many batched workloads; tail latency under concurrent streaming workloads can be higher depending on kernel/compilation.
- L4 / T4: not recommended for sustained 13B chat at your concurrency targets — good for inference-lite or smaller models.

Recommended starting config for validation:
- Hardware: H100 (2 x 80GB per shard) — helps with KV cache sharing and reduces cross-shard comms for chat workloads.
- Reserved throughput: provision for 450 req/min guaranteed with automatic burst to 650 req/min (we can tune after replay).
- Per-instance concurrency: 12–16 concurrent open sessions per shard (we'll tune based on sample trace).
- Streaming tuning: enable low-latency first-byte path, target 200–250 ms p95 for first byte during bursts.

Validation plan (short):
1) Synthetic baseline: run 10k synthetic requests across token-size buckets (32/128/256/512/1k) to collect p50/p95/p99 and throughput curves.
2) Live-sample replay: replay the trace you provide with identical inter-arrival times.
3) Streaming check: run 1:1 streaming sessions to validate first-byte latency and partial-token behavior.
4) Cost/throughput report: we will produce a short report with recommended reserved capacity and expected monthly cost delta between A100 and H100.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_worksheet.xlsx, validation-run-playbook.md

Proposed schedule: Mar 2, 10:00 AM PST start — we'll run the baseline first day and live replay on day two. Can you confirm access (IP allowlist / token) and whether you prefer a Zoom or Teams call for the kickoff?

Thanks — I'll loop Aditya for the benchmarking details.

--
Marissa

Adding technical notes from infra/bench team:
- We'll provision a temporary H100 pool (3 shards with 2x80GB each) for the validation window. That should allow us to test both single-shard and cross-shard behavior.
- Test matrix we'll run: concurrency sweep (1/8/16/32), batch-size sweep (1/2/4/8), token-length buckets as Marissa outlined.
- Streaming: we have a low-latency first-byte path configured; we'll instrument client-side jitter and measure from edge to first-byte.
- Logging: we'll capture per-token latency histograms, GPU util, KV cache hit rates; redacted logs will be shared.

Attachments: gpu-benchmark-config.json (contains the test parameters and metrics to capture).
